images.title: Neighbours that add to squares
images.purpose: Shows the row 3, 6, 10, 15 where each pair of neighbours adds to a perfect square: 9, 16 and 25.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One horizontal row of four number tiles across the middle, with an arc over each neighbouring pair.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 4 square tiles of equal size in one horizontal row, reading 3, 6, 10 and 15, filled teal (#0072B2) with white digits. Exactly 3 amber (#E69F00) arcs above the row, each joining one pair of neighbours, with its sum written at the top of the arc in reddish purple (#CC79A7): 9 over 3 and 6, 16 over 6 and 10, 25 over 10 and 15. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In a square pairs row, every two neighbours add up to a perfect square.

image_decisions.why: Arcs over neighbouring tiles show the puzzle's rule before students try 1 to 17.
